::: {.callout-note title="Calculations – 🧪 Phytoplankton" collapse="true"}

$$
C_{\mathrm{feeding}}^{\mathrm{jar}} = \text{carbon required per jar per day (mg C day}^{-1}\text{)}
$$

$$
V^{\mathrm{jar}} = \text{volume of each Daphnia jar (L)}
$$

$$
C_{\mathrm{total}} = N_{\mathrm{jars}} \times C_{\mathrm{jar}}
$$

Every phytoplankton species is grown at three vessel scales — stock flask, stock bottle, and experimental bottle — with the same number of replicate vessels (`Phyto_vessels_per_species`) kept at each scale, so the vessel count carries straight through from stock flasks up to experimental bottles once multiplied by the number of species. That vessel count, together with how much liquid a stock bottle and an experimental bottle each hold, sets how much COMBO medium has to be prepared in advance to fill every one of them once — not counting the medium used to top them up between transfers, which is handled separately in the [COMBO protocol](protocol/1_create_COMBO.md) — and, given how much volume comes out of a single batch, how many batches that requires.

```{r}
#| label: calculations_phytoplankton_vessels

Phyto_experimental_bottle_nr <- Phyto_species_count * Phyto_vessels_per_species
Phyto_stock_flask_nr <- Phyto_experimental_bottle_nr
Phyto_stock_bottle_nr <- Phyto_experimental_bottle_nr

COMBO_total_litres <- (
  (Phyto_stock_bottle_nr * Phyto_stock_bottle_liquid_mL) +
  (Phyto_experimental_bottle_nr * Phyto_experimental_bottle_liquid_mL)
  ) / 1000

COMBO_batches <- ceiling(COMBO_total_litres / COMBO_batch_volume_litres)
```

- **Experimental bottles:** `r Phyto_experimental_bottle_nr`
- **Stock bottles:** `r Phyto_stock_bottle_nr`
- **Stock flasks:** `r Phyto_stock_flask_nr`
- **COMBO medium needed:** `r round(COMBO_total_litres, 1)` L (`r COMBO_batches` batches)
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Calculations – 🦐 Daphnia" collapse="true"}

*Chaoborus*' worst-case daily appetite sets how many *Daphnia* neonates have to be available every day. How many jars that takes — `Daphnia_jars_per_cohort` per cohort, with `Daphnia_cohorts_in_rotation` cohorts of staggered ages running in parallel — is still a placeholder in [Parameters](4_parameters.qmd), pending the cohort-sizing and *Daphnia* propagation planning; multiplying the two gives how many cohort jars have to already be in place on day one.

```{r}
#| label: calculations_daphnia

Chaoborus_Daphnia_neonates_needed_per_day <- (
  Chaoborus_larvae_per_jar *
  Chaoborus_Daphnia_neonates_eaten_max_recorded *
  Treatments *
  Replicates
  )

Daphnia_jars_needed_at_start <- (
  Daphnia_jars_per_cohort *
  Daphnia_cohorts_in_rotation
  )
```

- **Cohorts in rotation:** `r Daphnia_cohorts_in_rotation`
- **Neonates needed per day:** `r Chaoborus_Daphnia_neonates_needed_per_day`
- **Jars per cohort:** `r Daphnia_jars_per_cohort`
- **Cohort jars needed at start:** `r Daphnia_jars_needed_at_start`
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Calculations – ☠️ Toxins" collapse="true"}

Whether the toxin dose given to *Chaoborus* is even measurable sets a lower bound on how much *Chaoborus* biomass has to be sampled. The ELISA kit's detection limit, converted to a mass via the volume each sample gets extracted into, gives the smallest amount of microcystin that can be detected at all; and since that toxin biodilutes twice on its way up the food chain — first from phytoplankton into *Daphnia*, then from *Daphnia* into *Chaoborus* — dividing the detectable mass by how little microcystin actually reaches a gram of *Chaoborus* dry weight gives the minimum biomass a sample needs to contain enough toxin to detect.

```{r}
#| label: calculations_toxins

Microcystins_minimum_detectable_mg <- (
  Microcystins_detection_limit_ug_per_L *
  (Microcystins_extraction_volume_mL / 1000) / 1000)

Microcystins_mg_per_g_DW_Chaoborus <- (
  Microcystins_mg_per_g_DW_phytoplankton /
  (Microcystins_biodilution_factor_Daphnia * Microcystins_biodilution_factor_Chaoborus))

Biomass_needed_for_toxins_mg <- (
  Microcystins_minimum_detectable_mg /
  Microcystins_mg_per_g_DW_Chaoborus) * 1000
```

- **Minimum detectable toxin mass:** `r round(Microcystins_minimum_detectable_mg * 1e6, 3)` ng
- **Microcystin reaching *Chaoborus*:** `r signif(Microcystins_mg_per_g_DW_Chaoborus, 3)` mg/g DW
- **Biomass needed for detection:** `r round(Biomass_needed_for_toxins_mg, 2)` mg
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Calculations – 🦟 Chaoborus" collapse="true"}

With one jar per treatment-by-replicate combination, the total biomass a single *Chaoborus* sample needs to cover every planned analysis — fatty acids, sterols, stoichiometry, and toxins — sets, via a single larva's dry weight, how many larvae one measurement requires; inflating that by the worst-case dead-to-alive ratio makes sure enough larvae still survive to be measured, and scaling up by every treatment-by-replicate jar gives the total larvae needed across the whole experiment. *(Whether this is sized for one measurement or for all of them still needs to be checked.)* That larvae total, together with how many neonates a single jar can get through at the worst-case single-feeding rate, in turn sets how many small stock jars — and the large adult jars that feed them — are needed to keep *Chaoborus* supplied.

```{r}
#| label: calculations_chaoborus

Jars_Chaoborus <- Treatments * Replicates

Biomass_needed_total_mg <- (
  DW_needed_for_PUFAs_mg +
  DW_needed_for_sterols_mg +
  DW_needed_for_N_and_C_mg +
  Biomass_needed_for_toxins_mg
  )

Chaoborus_one_measurement <- ceiling(
  (Biomass_needed_total_mg /
  Chaoborus_third_instar_DW_mg) *
  Chaoborus_dead_to_alive_ratio_worst_treatment
  )

Chaoborus_total <- Chaoborus_one_measurement * Treatments * Replicates

Daphnia_neonates_needed_per_jar_per_day <- Chaoborus_Daphnia_neonates_eaten_max_recorded * Chaoborus_larvae_per_jar

Jars_small_Daphnia <- ceiling(
  Chaoborus_total / (Daphnia_offsprings_per_mother_per_5_days / Chaoborus_Daphnia_neonates_eaten_per_day)
  )

Jars_big_Daphnia <- ceiling(
  Jars_small_Daphnia / (Daphnia_cohorts_adults_per_jar * Daphnia_offsprings_per_mother_per_5_days)
  )
```

- **Jars:** `r Jars_Chaoborus`
- **Biomass needed per sample:** `r round(Biomass_needed_total_mg, 2)` mg
- **Larvae needed per measurement:** `r Chaoborus_one_measurement`
- **Total larvae needed:** `r Chaoborus_total`
- **Neonates needed per jar per day:** `r Daphnia_neonates_needed_per_jar_per_day`
- **Small *Daphnia* stock jars:** `r Jars_small_Daphnia`
- **Large *Daphnia* stock jars:** `r Jars_big_Daphnia`
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Calculations – 🧪 Phytoplankton feeding demand" collapse="true"}

*(This section still needs revision.)* Once the *Daphnia* jar counts above are fixed, the total carbon those jars need each day follows directly from how many jars there are and how much carbon each is fed; splitting that demand across phytoplankton species in the same proportions as the diet mixes (averaged across treatments) gives each species' daily carbon target — plus, for *T. obliquus*, the extra carbon the untreated stock jars need on top of their share of the cohort diets. Checking that target against how much carbon a single experimental bottle can hold at its target concentration gives the fraction of that bottle harvested on the one day per rotation it supplies — alternating the daily harvest across the `Phyto_vessels_per_species` experimental bottles means only one bottle is drawn down at a time while the others regrow, with the harvested volume replaced by fresh COMBO on the spot (as in `protocol/4_feed_Daphnia.md`). These fractions only confirm the demand fits under a bottle's maximum carbon content; they don't yet confirm a diluted bottle actually regrows that far before its next harvest (see To do below).

```{r}
#| label: calculations_phytoplankton_feeding

Daphnia_cohort_carbon_mg_per_day <- (
  Daphnia_jars_needed_at_start *
  Large_jar_liquid_litres *
  Daphnia_algae_C_ad_libitum_mg_per_L_per_day
  )

Daphnia_stock_carbon_mg_per_day <- (
  (Jars_big_Daphnia *
  Large_jar_liquid_litres +
  Jars_small_Daphnia *
  Small_jar_liquid_litres) * Daphnia_algae_C_ad_libitum_mg_per_L_per_day)

Phyto_Microcystis_mg_C_per_day <- Daphnia_cohort_carbon_mg_per_day * mean(Diet_Microcystis_fraction)
Phyto_Synechococcus_mg_C_per_day <- Daphnia_cohort_carbon_mg_per_day * mean(Diet_Synechococcus_fraction)
Phyto_Nannochloropsis_mg_C_per_day <- Daphnia_cohort_carbon_mg_per_day * mean(Diet_Nannochloropsis_fraction)
Phyto_Tetradesmus_mg_C_per_day <- Daphnia_cohort_carbon_mg_per_day * mean(Diet_Tetradesmus_fraction) +
  Daphnia_stock_carbon_mg_per_day

Phyto_experimental_bottle_max_mg_C <- (Phyto_experimental_bottle_liquid_mL / 1000) *
  Phyto_experimental_bottle_highest_mg_C_per_L

Phyto_Microcystis_harvest_fraction <- Phyto_Microcystis_mg_C_per_day / Phyto_experimental_bottle_max_mg_C
Phyto_Synechococcus_harvest_fraction <- Phyto_Synechococcus_mg_C_per_day / Phyto_experimental_bottle_max_mg_C
Phyto_Nannochloropsis_harvest_fraction <- Phyto_Nannochloropsis_mg_C_per_day / Phyto_experimental_bottle_max_mg_C
Phyto_Tetradesmus_harvest_fraction <- Phyto_Tetradesmus_mg_C_per_day / Phyto_experimental_bottle_max_mg_C
```

- **_Daphnia_ cohort carbon demand:** `r round(Daphnia_cohort_carbon_mg_per_day, 1)` mg C/day
- **_Daphnia_ stock carbon demand:** `r round(Daphnia_stock_carbon_mg_per_day, 1)` mg C/day
- **_M. aeruginosa_:** `r round(Phyto_Microcystis_mg_C_per_day, 1)` mg C/day (`r round(Phyto_Microcystis_harvest_fraction * 100, 1)`% of bottle)
- **_S. elongatus_:** `r round(Phyto_Synechococcus_mg_C_per_day, 1)` mg C/day (`r round(Phyto_Synechococcus_harvest_fraction * 100, 1)`% of bottle)
- **_N. limnetica_:** `r round(Phyto_Nannochloropsis_mg_C_per_day, 1)` mg C/day (`r round(Phyto_Nannochloropsis_harvest_fraction * 100, 1)`% of bottle)
- **_T. obliquus_:** `r round(Phyto_Tetradesmus_mg_C_per_day, 1)` mg C/day (`r round(Phyto_Tetradesmus_harvest_fraction * 100, 1)`% of bottle)
:::

::: {.callout-note title="Calculations – 🪜 Infrastructure" collapse="true"}

Every jar in the experiment — *Chaoborus* jars, and both the small and large *Daphnia* stock jars — has a known weight once filled, so totalling those up and spreading the load evenly across the available shelves gives how much each shelf has to carry, rounded up to a whole kilogram.

```{r}
#| label: calculations_infrastructure

Weight_per_shelf_kg <- ceiling(
  (
    (Large_jar_with_liquid_kg * Jars_Chaoborus) +
    (Small_jar_with_liquid_kg * Jars_small_Daphnia) +
    (Large_jar_with_liquid_kg * Jars_big_Daphnia)
    ) / Shelves
)
```

- **Weight per shelf:** `r Weight_per_shelf_kg` kg
:::
